issue.title: Bug: Truthy string breaks if stmts in QOS SAI tests

failure.body:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

Critical

### Description of the bug

PR #24668 adds a truthy string to some of the conditions in the test cases here:
```diff
-            if hwsku in ('DellEMC-Z9332f-M-O16C64', 'DellEMC-Z9332f-O32') or 'Arista-7060X6' in hwsku:
+            if hwsku in ('DellEMC-Z9332f-M-O16C64', 'DellEMC-Z9332f-O32') or 'Arista-7060X6' \
+                    or 'Nokia-IXR7220-H6' in hwsku:
```

This causes the condition to evaluate to True always since the "in hwsku" was dropped for "Arista-7060X6".

### Steps to Reproduce

Run test_qos_sai.py tests on latest master.

### Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior

Actual behavior: Unexpected variables being used:
```
ERROR: sai_qos_tests.PFCXonTest
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/root/saitests/py3/sai_qos_tests.py", line 3234, in runTest
    (pkts_num_egr_mem + pkts_num_leak_out + pkts_num_trig_pfc -
     ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for +: 'NoneType' and 'int'

----------------------------------------------------------------------
Ran 1 test in 16.207s
```

Expected:
Test pass

### Relevant log output

```shell
ERROR: sai_qos_tests.PFCXonTest
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/root/saitests/py3/sai_qos_tests.py", line 3234, in runTest
    (pkts_num_egr_mem + pkts_num_leak_out + pkts_num_trig_pfc -
     ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for +: 'NoneType' and 'int'

----------------------------------------------------------------------
Ran 1 test in 16.207s
```


resolution.title: Fix incorrect truthy string condition in PFCXonTest
resolution.description:
## Description of PR

### Summary

This PR fixes the incorrect conditional expression in `PFCXonTest`.

Previously, the condition used the string literal `'Arista-7060X6'` directly in an `or` expression. Since non-empty strings are always truthy in Python, the condition could evaluate incorrectly and lead to unintended execution.

This change replaces the string literal with an explicit membership check:

```python
'Arista-7060X6' in hwsku
```

This ensures the condition is evaluated correctly based on the hardware SKU.

### Testing

- Verified that the code change is syntactically correct.
- Confirmed the condition now performs an explicit membership check instead of relying on a truthy string.

Fixes #25791
